label: DISTANCE

cover.headline: When he goes quiet: *5 things to try* first

points.heading: Notice the story you’re telling
points.body: Silence leaves a gap, and worry fills it fast. Separate what you know from what you’re guessing.
points.panel: Ask yourself: what do I actually know right now?

points.heading: Say what you see, gently
points.body: Describe it without accusing. An observation is easier to answer than a charge.
points.panel: “You’ve seemed quiet this week. I’ve noticed, and I care.”

points.heading: Offer a door, not a deadline
points.body: Some people need time before they can talk. Let him know you’re ready when he is.
points.panel: “I’m here when you feel like talking. No rush.”

points.heading: Keep the small things warm
points.body: A quiet stretch doesn’t have to mean a cold house. A coffee made or a hand on his shoulder still counts.
points.panel: Do one small kind thing today, no strings attached.

points.heading: Ask what would help
points.body: You don’t have to guess what he needs. Asking is kinder than assuming.
points.panel: “Is there anything that would make this week easier?”

close.save: Save this for the next quiet spell.

caption:
When someone you love goes quiet, your mind writes the rest of the story, and it rarely picks the kind version.

Before you act on that story, try one of these. They won’t pry anyone open, and they aren’t meant to. They keep the door open while he finds his words.

Share this with a friend who’s in a quiet season, and follow @spotseason for more.
